synopsis: NHTSA opened Preliminary Evaluation PE22-003 on 21 February 2022 after 278 complaints alleging inadvertent Honda Collision Mitigation Braking System activation, including 107 Accord and 171 CR-V complaints [f1483, f15760]. Six complaints alleged a collision, and some reported large speed changes despite nothing obstructing the vehicle’s path [f15760]. In April 2024, NHTSA upgraded the case to Engineering Analysis EA24-002, investigating false automatic braking across 2,997,604 vehicles, covering 2018–2022 Accord and Accord Hybrid and 2017–2022 CR-V and CR-V Hybrid [f1485, f10422, f15761]. The glossary reports 1,294 complaints at that stage; these complaint and vehicle totals cover both model families, not the Accord alone, and the supplied facts report investigation activity rather than a final finding [f15761, f1485, f10422].
